transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello. I came in today because, honestly, I just feel like I cannot settle down inside my own skin anymore. It's the most exhausting thing. It actually reminds me of this awful wool sweater my sister knitted for me back in the eighties. Oh, she was always knitting something, usually in these hideous mustard colors. She used to live up in Vermont, which makes sense for heavy wool, but she moved down to Florida and kept knitting them anyway. 

But anyway, I just have this feeling like I have to jump up and do the next thing, you know? Even when I am completely worn out to the bone and I know I should just be sitting still. Like yesterday, I was trying to sit in my recliner—it's one of those nice plush ones, we got it on sale at Macy's right before they closed the one at our mall. It's a shame about the malls, really, all the stores are empty and people just buy things on their phones now. I don't even know how they see the pictures on those tiny screens. 

What was I saying? Oh, right. The chair. I just can't sit still in it, even when I'm dead tired. I just keep having to jump up.
Are you currently taking any medications, especially any antipsychotic or psychiatric medications, and if so, when did you start them?

No, no medications like that. I don't take any of those psychiatric pills or antipsychotics or whatever you called them. I used to take a little water pill for my ankles, but my regular doctor took me off that last year. He said I didn't need it anymore, which was a relief because, let me tell you, having to run to the bathroom every five minutes when you're trying to get through the grocery store is just a nightmare. 

And the grocery store is already so stressful these days! Have you seen the prices? I went in for a carton of eggs the other day and nearly had a heart attack right there in the dairy aisle. Three dollars and fifty cents for a dozen eggs! It used to be you could get them for under a dollar. My neighbor, Shirley—she lives in the blue house at the end of the cul-de-sac with all those awful plastic flamingos in the yard—she told me she started buying powdered eggs online. Powdered eggs! I told her, "Shirley, I don't care how much they cost, I am not eating something that comes out of a packet and tastes like cardboard." 

But no, to answer your question, I don't take any of those medications you mentioned. Just my vitamins, really. I take a multivitamin and some fish oil, though I don't know if the fish oil actually does anything. It just gives me the burps.
Is this feeling of needing to constantly move and being unable to sit still something new that started recently, or has it been a lifelong pattern for you since childhood?

Oh, goodness, no, it's not new at all. It's really been my whole life. I mean, even back in grade school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was bright but just careless. I was always losing my papers, talking out of turn, and they were constantly having to remind me to stay in my seat or just finish my schoolwork. 

I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable... oh, she was a piece of work. She had this towering beehive hairdo that must have taken a whole can of hairspray every single morning. You could smell the Aqua Net from all the way down the hall! It's a wonder any of us could breathe in that classroom. Actually, my late husband used to joke that her generation is the whole reason we have a hole in the ozone layer. He was always watching those nature documentaries on PBS. You know, the ones with that British man narrating? What's his name... David Attenborough! Such a soothing voice. I could listen to him talk about penguins or the rainforest for hours. 

Although, to be honest, I'd probably still be getting up and pacing around the living room while I watched it. But yes... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, if it started recently. No, it's always been exactly like this.

Have there been specific periods, lasting several days or more, when this restlessness got much worse and was accompanied by feeling unusually happy, energetic, or needing much less sleep than usual, followed by times when you felt more like your normal self?

Unusually happy? Oh, heavens no. I mean, who is unusually happy these days anyway? You turn on the television and it's just one awful thing after another. My sister Brenda, the one down in Florida who knits those sweaters, she leaves the twenty-four-hour news channel on all day long. Just blaring in the living room. I told her she is going to give herself an ulcer listening to those politicians yell at each other. She says it keeps her company since her husband passed, but I just can't stand the noise. I much prefer the Game Show Network. Family Feud is always a hoot. That Steve Harvey, he makes the funniest faces, doesn't he? He just stares right at the camera when someone gives a ridiculous answer. I really don't know where they find some of those contestants, honestly. They must screen them just to find the goofiest ones. 

But... wait, what did you ask me? Something about sleep? Oh, right, needing less sleep or feeling energetic. No, no, nothing like that. I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get my seven hours, I am just a total wreck the next day. The restlessness doesn't really come and go in spells like you're saying, it is just always there. Every single day. I never have days where I feel on top of the world or don't need to sleep, if that's what you mean.
